title: Germany-first student discovery: audience sizing and economics

queries.query: site.daad.de Indian students Germany 2025 2026 59000 first semester

findings.claim: Indian international enrolment (Bildungsausländer) was 69,076 in winter 2025/26, versus 58,833 in 2024/25. These are stocks, not annual new entrants.
findings.label: Data
findings.confidence: High for the defined statistic; not a product TAM

findings.implication: A substantial existing corridor warrants investigation. Do not count enrolled students as fresh yearly prospects, add stock to applicant flow, or multiply the count by a hypothetical price.

findings.implication: This annual channel measure is more relevant than enrolled stock for recruitment research, but excludes other application routes and unconverted aspirants. It is neither the complete prospective market nor a measured reachable SAM.

findings.claim: In winter 2024/25, 49.9% of international degree-seeking students were in master’s programmes and 36.8% in bachelor’s programmes. These shares cover all origins, not India specifically.
findings.label: Data
findings.confidence: High for the broad population; Low for an India-specific mix

sources.title: Costs of education and living
sources.date: Undated live page; proof section explicitly says 2025; checked 2026-10-25

findings.implication: Financial proof is not an all-inclusive degree budget. The founder’s ₹10 lakh example cannot by itself establish affordability; avoid INR comparisons without a dated exchange rate and programme/city/duration-specific costs.

findings.claim: DAAD’s current guidance indicates €900–€1,200 monthly living costs and €70–€430 semester contributions. It identifies tuition exceptions, including non-EU charges in Baden-Württemberg and institution-specific Bavarian fees.
findings.label: Data
findings.sourceDate: Undated live guidance checked 2026-10-25; do not use its older 2023 survey averages as current costs
findings.confidence: Medium as general planning ranges; exact local costs require fresh sources

sources.title: Costs of education and living
sources.date: Undated live page; proof section explicitly says 2025; checked 2026-10-25

findings.implication: Separate tuition, semester contributions, living costs, travel/setup, insurance, and contingency. Do not market Germany as universally free or use part-time work as guaranteed funding.

findings.claim: uni-assist handling fees are €75 for the first chosen course and €30 for each additional course in the same semester, including standard and VPD procedures.
findings.label: Data
findings.implication: A shortlist can create real application expenditure. Show applicable costs without suggesting an advisory charge replaces official fees; some institution-specific exceptions must be checked.

findings.claim: The founder has chosen a free launch and will fund initial costs. Student/parent payment around ₹500 per month or plan is a later, unvalidated hypothesis; no billing period is locked.
findings.label: Assumption
findings.confidence: High as a record of intent; Low as a business viability or willingness-to-pay claim

sources.title: Completed founder brief
sources.note: Primary for founder intent, not independent market demand

findings.implication: Launch paid revenue is ₹0 by design. Do not reuse agency subscriptions, compute paid TAM from aspirants, or present early free use as paid demand.

findings.claim: A paid TAM/SAM, realistic Year-1 obtainable audience, CAC, churn, and LTV cannot yet be estimated defensibly from the available evidence.
findings.label: Opinion
findings.confidence: High that these inputs remain unmeasured; no numerical forecast supplied

sources.title: Completed founder brief
sources.note: Primary for founder intent, not independent market demand

findings.implication: Use a scenario model with explicit inputs: reachable students × intake activation × useful-result completion. Measure returning users and cost per verified useful result, including model, data, review, and support costs. Do not treat chosen funnel inputs as benchmarks.

annualChannelProxy.not: all applicants, all aspiring students, admissions, or measured reachable SAM

audienceSizing.serviceableAudience: Unknown until initial subject, intake, outreach access, and data coverage are chosen.
audienceSizing.SOM: No forecast. Scenario formula only: reachable students × activation rate × useful-result completion rate. Each factor must be measured in a pilot.
audienceSizing.launchRevenueLabel: Founder-confirmed free-launch intent, not a market forecast
audienceSizing.futurePaidMarket: Not sized before evidence on willingness to pay and a defined billable outcome.

contradictions.detail: DAAD India’s 22 September 2025 page reports 59,419 students; WWO2026 reports 58,833 Bildungsausländer for winter 2024/25. These publications do not provide a directly reconciled classification on the accessed pages. Prefer the newer report’s explicit category and do not silently merge them.

gaps.gap: Complete annual Indian Germany aspirant population, by intended degree and field
gaps.why: Neither enrolled stock nor one processing channel counts all prospective users.
gaps.nextStep: Use official applicant breakdowns where available and primary recruitment measurement; do not invent an aspirant multiplier.

gaps.gap: Reachable initial cohort and conversion into useful results
gaps.why: No student pilot metrics are recorded.
gaps.nextStep: Measure an actual recruitment and use funnel before a Year-1 SOM forecast.

gaps.why: Broad international shares cannot be transferred to India.
gaps.nextStep: Request disaggregated official data or recruit separate cohorts; report sample limits.

gaps.gap: Paid willingness-to-pay, repeat usage, paid CAC/LTV/churn
gaps.why: Free-launch founder intent supplies none of these.
gaps.nextStep: Keep pricing scenarios labeled assumptions and run a later real payment test only after useful outcomes are demonstrated.

gaps.gap: Free-pilot unit cost and a spending cap
gaps.why: Actual model usage, data curation, verification time, support, and current founder capacity are unmeasured.
gaps.nextStep: Set a founder-funded cap and track cost per verified useful result; keep human work visible.

gaps.why: Official financial proof and general cost ranges do not establish full-degree affordability.
gaps.nextStep: Gather actual institution/city costs, duration, funding, and a dated exchange rate; show uncertainty.

redFlags: Do not claim the 69,076 enrolled stock or 26,185 uni-assist applicants are paid TAM, reachable users, or a reliable Year-1 forecast.
A free launch produces no paid-revenue validation; no evidence presently supports a paid market-size estimate.
Insufficient financial input cannot justify a best-country or affordability conclusion.
yellowFlags: Growth in the corridor is not evidence students will use or trust this particular product.
Official general cost guidance must be replaced by programme/city-specific evidence for personalised results.
The newest statistical release mixes reference periods; each number must retain its own period and population definition.
Press coverage and the source report share one data lineage; do not count them as independent datasets.
summary: The Germany corridor is measurable and active, and a current annual processing-channel proxy is available. The product’s reachable audience and economics remain unvalidated. Lead the free pilot with useful-result, return-use, and cost metrics; avoid a revenue TAM constructed from enrolments.
